gaps.rationale: A fast skeletal-muscle troponin sensitizer could transiently improve force generation in SMA patients whose weakness is partly caused by surviving motor neurons being unable to activate muscle effectively.
gaps.caveat: The cited evidence is from a myasthenia-gravis model and does not establish benefit in denervated or atrophic SMA muscle, while systemic effects and long-term safety require evaluation.
gaps.experiment: First conduct a muscle-biopsy or isolated-muscle study using SMA patient-derived fibers to determine whether CK-2017357 increases contractile force at physiologic activation levels.

mechanism_evidence: "Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder of motor neurons that manifests with weakness caused by widespread skeletal muscle denervation atrophy." (PMID:38330285, P8)
"The systemic scAAV9 therapy mediated complete correction of motor function, prevented MN death and rescued the weight loss phenotype close to normal" (PMID:22047105, P50)
intervention_evidence: "Histological analyses revealed that significantly fewer motor neurons were lost in caffeine-treated mice at p41, despite no changes in soma morphology." (PMID:40931339, P4)
gaps.rationale: Caffeine is a readily available systemic compound with a plausible neuroprotective or symptomatic-testing rationale in a motor-neuron disease, and the supplied evidence reports reduced motor-neuron loss in mice.
gaps.caveat: The evidence does not specify the model or establish preservation of SMN function or meaningful clinical benefit in SMA, and adverse cardiovascular and stimulant effects may limit dosing.
gaps.experiment: First test caffeine in a severe SMN-deficient mouse model with blinded motor-neuron counts, neuromuscular-function measurements, survival, and tolerability monitoring.

mechanism_evidence: "CK-2127107 helps increase skeletal muscle contractility and enhances physical performance in patients with neuromuscular diseases." (PMID:27490705, P39)

"Peripheral motor neuropathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) cause motor neuron damage and death, straining the ability of surviving motor neurons to stimulate muscle effectively to generate force" (PMID:22344294, P4)
intervention_evidence: "Here, we studied the ability of the novel fast skeletal muscle troponin activator, CK-2066260, to augment force generation at submaximal calcium levels" (PMID:23572184, P2)
gaps.rationale: CK-2066260 is a fast skeletal-muscle troponin activator with direct in-vitro support for increasing force at submaximal calcium, making it a plausible symptomatic adjunct for SMA weakness.
gaps.caveat: Benefit may be limited by severe denervation and muscle atrophy, and the compound's pharmacokinetics, systemic tolerability, and clinical development status require verification before patient use.
gaps.experiment: First test CK-2066260 in SMA patient-derived muscle fibers and a severe-SMA animal model, measuring force, fatigue resistance, motor-neuron preservation, and adverse effects.

mechanism_evidence: "CK-2127107 helps increase skeletal muscle contractility and enhances physical performance in patients with neuromuscular diseases." (PMID:27490705, P39)

"Peripheral motor neuropathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) cause motor neuron damage and death, straining the ability of surviving motor neurons to stimulate muscle effectively to generate force" (PMID:22344294, P4)
intervention_evidence: "In contrast, MyoMed‐205 treated rats had markedly improved diastolic function, less myocardial fibrosis, reduced SKM myopathy, and increased SKM function." (PMID:35301823, P4)
gaps.rationale: MyoMed-205 may address downstream skeletal-muscle dysfunction, but the quoted study is in rats with cardiac and general myopathy rather than selective evidence in SMA.
gaps.caveat: The intervention's composition, mechanism, dosing, and relevance to primary motor-neuron disease are insufficiently established from the supplied evidence.
gaps.experiment: First characterize MyoMed-205 in SMA patient-derived muscle myotubes and severe-SMA animals using force measurements, muscle histology, and motor-neuron survival endpoints.

mechanism_evidence: "Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder of motor neurons that manifests with weakness caused by widespread skeletal muscle denervation atrophy." (PMID:38330285, P8)
"The systemic scAAV9 therapy mediated complete correction of motor function, prevented MN death and rescued the weight loss phenotype close to normal" (PMID:22047105, P50)
intervention_evidence: "The T0901317-treated group spinal cord morphology demonstrates significant improvement, with a diameter approximating that of the wild-type group, indicating LXR agonist-mediated protection of spinal motor neurons." (PMID:42581247, P30)
gaps.rationale: T0901317 is an LXR agonist with a quoted protective effect on spinal motor neurons, but the mechanism and evidence are not directly tied to SMN1 deficiency.
gaps.caveat: LXR agonism can cause lipid, hepatic, and metabolic adverse effects, and the supplied spinal-cord morphology finding does not demonstrate functional rescue in SMA.
gaps.experiment: First assess T0901317 in SMN-deficient mice with motor-neuron survival, muscle strength, disease progression, and metabolic and hepatic safety endpoints.

mechanism_evidence: "Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder of motor neurons that manifests with weakness caused by widespread skeletal muscle denervation atrophy." (PMID:38330285, P8)
"The systemic scAAV9 therapy mediated complete correction of motor function, prevented MN death and rescued the weight loss phenotype close to normal" (PMID:22047105, P50)
intervention_evidence: "Concentration-dependent neuroprotective effects were demonstrated by IncuCyte SX5 (Figure 4, I–L) and LDH assay (Figure 4M), as evidenced by preserved neurite length, number of cell clusters, and reduced LDH release." (PMID:42275159, P17)
gaps.rationale: PF-04457845 is a clinically developed FAAH inhibitor with reported neurite and cell-cluster preservation, providing a weak exploratory neuroprotection hypothesis for SMA.
gaps.caveat: The evidence is primarily in vitro and does not show rescue of SMN-dependent motor-neuron degeneration, while systemic FAAH inhibition can produce adverse neuropsychiatric and hepatic effects.
gaps.experiment: First test PF-04457845 in SMN-deficient motor-neuron cultures and mice, measuring SMN-dependent motor-neuron survival and in vivo strength with safety monitoring.

mechanism_evidence: "Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder of motor neurons that manifests with weakness caused by widespread skeletal muscle denervation atrophy." (PMID:38330285, P8)
"The systemic scAAV9 therapy mediated complete correction of motor function, prevented MN death and rescued the weight loss phenotype close to normal" (PMID:22047105, P50)
gaps.intervention_edge: Enterococcus faecium rescues motor neuron degeneration
intervention_evidence: "Animals fed E. faecium showed reduced motor neuron degeneration under oxidative stress compared to those maintained on a standard Escherichia coli diet." (PMID:41616251, P2)
gaps.rationale: Enterococcus faecium could indirectly modify oxidative-stress or microbiome-related processes that contribute to motor-neuron injury, but this is a remote and nonspecific rationale for SMA.
gaps.caveat: The quoted reduction in motor-neuron degeneration under oxidative stress does not establish efficacy in SMN-deficient animals, and live-biotherapy use raises infection, colonization, and safety concerns in vulnerable patients.
gaps.experiment: First test the intervention in an SMN-deficient mouse model with blinded motor-neuron survival, muscle function, microbiome, infection-safety, and systemic toxicity endpoints.

mechanism_evidence: "Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive neuromuscular disorder of motor neurons that manifests with weakness caused by widespread skeletal muscle denervation atrophy." (PMID:38330285, P8)
"The systemic scAAV9 therapy mediated complete correction of motor function, prevented MN death and rescued the weight loss phenotype close to normal" (PMID:22047105, P50)
intervention_evidence: "These data indicate that site-targeted C3 inhibition substantially attenuates the progressive MN loss that underlies functional decline in this model." (PMID:42492371, P26)
gaps.rationale: C3 inhibition is a plausible way to modulate complement-mediated inflammatory or degenerative motor-neuron injury and the quoted report describes reduced motor-neuron loss in a model.
gaps.caveat: CR2Crry is a specialized biologic construct whose delivery, pharmacokinetics, and mechanism are unclear, and complement blockade may impair host defense or cause other immune-related toxicity.
gaps.experiment: First evaluate CR2Crry in an SMN-deficient motor-neuron system and severe-SMA animal model, assessing motor-neuron survival, strength, and innate immune safety.

mechanism_evidence: "CK-2127107 helps increase skeletal muscle contractility and enhances physical performance in patients with neuromuscular diseases." (PMID:27490705, P39)

"Peripheral motor neuropathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) cause motor neuron damage and death, straining the ability of surviving motor neurons to stimulate muscle effectively to generate force" (PMID:22344294, P4)
gaps.intervention_edge: recombinant wild-type troponin C rescues skeletal muscle contractility
intervention_evidence: "the contractile dysfunction of myofibers from patients was repaired by replacing endogenous, mutant TnC with recombinant, wild-type TnC." (PMID:33755597, P2)

literature.query: (TITLE_ABS:"recombinant wild-type troponin C") AND (TITLE_ABS:"spinal muscular atrophy")

gaps.rationale: Replacing defective troponin C would be mechanistically relevant only to selected muscular or neuromuscular disorders and does not correct the primary SMN deficiency in SMA.
gaps.caveat: The in-vitro repair used patient fibers carrying mutant TnC, and a recombinant cytosolic protein would face delivery, stability, immunogenicity, and target-population limitations in SMA.
gaps.experiment: First test recombinant wild-type troponin C in SMA patient-derived muscle fibers to determine whether a TnC-related contractile defect is actually present before animal studies.

mechanism_evidence: "CK-2127107 helps increase skeletal muscle contractility and enhances physical performance in patients with neuromuscular diseases." (PMID:27490705, P39)

"Peripheral motor neuropathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) cause motor neuron damage and death, straining the ability of surviving motor neurons to stimulate muscle effectively to generate force" (PMID:22344294, P4)
intervention_evidence: "a single intravenous AAV9-delivered amiR-SOD1 robustly silences hSOD1 in the CNS and peripheral tissues, preserves neuromuscular function, and markedly extends survival in ALS mice." (PMID:42350385, P4)

literature_core.query: (TITLE_ABS:"amir sod1") AND (TITLE_ABS:"spinal muscular atrophy") AND (TITLE_ABS:"gene therapy" OR TITLE_ABS:"adeno-associated" OR TITLE_ABS:"gene transfer")

gaps.rationale: AAV9-amiR-SOD1 is an ALS-specific SOD1-silencing therapy and does not address the established SMN1/SMN deficiency mechanism of SMA.
gaps.caveat: Its quoted efficacy is restricted to SOD1-associated disease, making extrapolation to genetically heterogeneous SMA a mechanism mismatch.
gaps.experiment: No SMA-specific experiment is justified for this intervention; first establish the target mechanism and genetic population in which SOD1 silencing could be relevant.

mechanism_evidence: "CK-2127107 helps increase skeletal muscle contractility and enhances physical performance in patients with neuromuscular diseases." (PMID:27490705, P39)

"Peripheral motor neuropathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) cause motor neuron damage and death, straining the ability of surviving motor neurons to stimulate muscle effectively to generate force" (PMID:22344294, P4)
gaps.intervention_edge: soluble activin type IIB-receptor applicable_to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
intervention_evidence: "the inhibition of the myostatin/activin A pathway can also reverse muscle loss in other diseases such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy [89,90,91,92], metabolic diseases" (PMID:32605273, P78)

literature.query: (TITLE_ABS:"soluble activin type IIB-receptor" OR TITLE_ABS:"ActRIIB-Fc" OR TITLE_ABS:"sActRIIB" OR TITLE_ABS:"sActRIIB-Fc") AND (TITLE_ABS:"spinal muscular atrophy")

gaps.rationale: Blocking activin/myostatin signaling could reduce pathological muscle loss and potentially improve strength in SMA, a disease with substantial secondary muscle atrophy and wasting.
gaps.caveat: The supplied evidence is a review-level extrapolation from ALS and other diseases, and systemic ActRIIB blockade may cause immune, bone, metabolic, or muscle-related adverse effects without improving motor-neuron survival.
gaps.experiment: First evaluate a soluble activin type IIB receptor in SMA patient-derived muscle cultures and an SMN-deficient animal model, measuring muscle mass, force, disease progression, and safety.

papers.title: Nusinersen initiated in infants during the presymptomatic stage of spinal muscular atrophy: Interim efficacy and safety results from the Phase 2 NURTURE study.
papers.summary: In the ongoing single-arm NURTURE trial, presymptomatic infants with genetically confirmed spinal muscular atrophy who received nusinersen retained motor abilities, remained alive without permanent ventilation, and showed sustained motor-function gains over a median 2.9 years. Plasma and CSF phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain levels declined during nusinersen's loading period, while ulnar and peroneal compound muscle action potential amplitudes remained stable; interpretation is limited by the small, uncontrolled study.
papers.why: This clinical trial directly demonstrates efficacy and safety of presymptomatic nusinersen treatment in infants with SMA.

papers.title: Onasemnogene abeparvovec for presymptomatic infants with two copies of SMN2 at risk for spinal muscular atrophy type 1: the Phase III SPR1NT trial.
papers.summary: In the single-arm Phase III SPR1NT trial, one-time intravenous onasemnogene abeparvovec given to 14 presymptomatic infants with biallelic SMN1 deletions and two SMN2 copies was associated with motor development, ventilator-free survival, growth, swallowing, and respiratory independence through 18 months. Treatment was generally well tolerated, although transient treatment-related hepatotoxicity and mild thrombocytopenia occurred, and the small sample, external natural-history comparator, and exclusion of children with baseline CMAP below 2 mV limit the strength and generalizability of the findings.
papers.why: The Phase III SPR1NT study directly demonstrates gene-replacement efficacy in presymptomatic infants at risk for SMA type 1 and supports newborn screening and early intervention.

papers.title: Spinal muscular atrophy: From approved therapies to future therapeutic targets for personalized medicine.
papers.summary: This review finds that nusinersen, onasemnogene abeparvovec, and risdiplam improve survival, motor function, or disease milestones in spinal muscular atrophy by restoring or increasing SMN protein, but none is considered curative. It identifies numerous SMN-dependent and SMN-independent adjunctive approaches targeting splicing, neuronal protection, muscle, neuromuscular-junction, cytoskeletal, metabolic, autophagy, ubiquitin, apoptotic, and regenerative pathways, while highlighting several clinical null or mixed results and the need for early treatment and combination strategies.
papers.why: This SMA review summarizes three licensed SMN-restoring therapies and identifies adjunctive downstream and SMN-independent treatment strategies, although it is not itself a primary intervention study.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of Apitegromab in Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Types 2 and 3: The Phase 2 TOPAZ Study.
papers.summary: In the phase 2 TOPAZ study, monthly intravenous apitegromab, alone or with nusinersen, was associated with improved motor-function outcomes in younger participants with later-onset spinal muscular atrophy types 2 and 3, with the clearest gains in the younger nonambulatory type 2 cohort. Serum latent myostatin increased dose-dependently as a marker of myostatin-target engagement, and treatment was generally well tolerated over 12 months, although the small, mostly open-label study and background nusinersen treatment limit causal interpretation.
papers.why: The phase 2 TOPAZ trial directly tested apitegromab alone and with nusinersen in SMA types 2 and 3 and reports motor-function and safety data.

papers.title: An orally available, brain penetrant, small molecule lowers huntingtin levels by enhancing pseudoexon inclusion.
papers.summary: Branaplam is an oral, brain-penetrant splicing modulator that restores SMN2 exon 7 inclusion and was developed for spinal muscular atrophy type 1. The present study primarily evaluates its transferability in Huntington’s disease, showing branaplam-induced HTT pseudoexon 50a inclusion and HTT lowering in human cells, BacHD mice, and blood from infants with SMA type 1, thereby providing a human pharmacodynamic demonstration in the input disease population.
papers.why: The study provides mechanistic models and high-throughput assays for existing SMA splicing drugs, including dose-dependent specificity and synergy between risdiplam, branaplam, and other exon-inclusion therapies.

papers.title: Enhanced splicing modulation by NMA-modified antisense oligonucleotides.
papers.summary: The paper shows that NMA-modified splice-switching oligonucleotides, particularly the SMN2-targeting salanersen (NMA-3), correct SMN2 exon 7 splicing more potently than MOE-modified nusinersen in SMA patient fibroblasts and human SMN2 transgenic mice. NMA-3 produced durable CNS activity with an improved acute and delayed mouse tolerability profile, while the same chemistry also enhanced SCN1A exon 20N modulation in a transferable Dravet syndrome strategy.
papers.why: Reports a long-lasting NMA-modified SSO that is three- to four-fold more potent than nusinersen in human SMN2 transgenic mice.

papers.title: Advancing treatment of spinal muscular atrophy through inhibition of the myostatin signaling pathway.
papers.summary: This review discusses persistent skeletal muscle weakness in spinal muscular atrophy despite treatments that increase survival motor neuron (SMN) protein. It identifies inhibition of the myostatin signaling pathway as a potential complementary muscle-targeted approach, with preclinical and clinical data discussed, but the abstract does not report a demonstrated treatment effect in patients.
papers.why: The review summarizes existing preclinical and clinical myostatin-inhibitor approaches and motor-function endpoints that could complement SMN-directed therapies in SMA.

papers.title: Small Molecules in Development for the Treatment of Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: This review identifies spinal muscular atrophy as an SMN1-loss disease in which inadequate SMN2-derived SMN protein creates a therapeutically actionable deficiency. It describes repurposed and novel small molecules that increase SMN2 transcription, exon 7 inclusion, RNA or protein stability, or downstream motor-neuron and muscle function, but highlights inconsistent clinical benefit, toxicity, poor CNS penetration, and limited trial design as major barriers.
papers.why: This review directly catalogs repurposed and medicinal-chemistry-derived small molecules tested for SMA, including compounds that reached clinical development.

papers.title: Chemistry, structure and function of approved oligonucleotide therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review identifies three approved therapeutic approaches for spinal muscular atrophy: nusinersen-mediated SMN2 splice switching, onasemnogene abeparvovec gene replacement, and risdiplam-mediated small-molecule splicing modulation. It reports that these approaches increase full-length functional SMN production and describes clinical benefit from nusinersen including prolonged survival and improved motor development.
papers.why: The review describes clinically validated oligonucleotide chemistries and delivery strategies, including approved splice-switching treatment used in SMA.

papers.title: Peripheral SMN restoration is essential for long-term rescue of a severe spinal muscular atrophy mouse model.
papers.summary: Systemically administered ASO-10-27 markedly improved survival and disease-associated tissue, neuromuscular, and motor-function abnormalities in a severe mouse model of spinal muscular atrophy, outperforming intracerebroventricular delivery. The treatment increased SMN2 exon 7 inclusion and full-length SMN across tissues, restored circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 by rescuing hepatic Igfals expression, and implicated early liver dysfunction as a contributor to severe SMA pathogenesis.
papers.why: The severe mouse study shows that systemic ASO-10-27 restores SMN2 splicing, rescues survival, and normalizes a peripheral IGF1 abnormality.

papers.title: Current Clinical Applications of In Vivo Gene Therapy with AAVs.
papers.summary: This review reports that systemic AAV gene transfer targeting SMN1 can produce major functional benefit in infants with spinal muscular atrophy type 1, leading to approval of onasemnogene abeparvovec. Benefits include survival without permanent ventilation, improved CHOP-INTEND scores, and motor, respiratory, and oral milestone gains, while hepatotoxicity, treatment timing, and dorsal root ganglion inflammation remain important limitations.
papers.why: The review summarizes clinically available AAV gene therapy for SMA and reusable methods for in vivo vector delivery and neuromuscular gene transfer.

papers.title: Results from a phase 1 study of nusinersen (ISIS-SMN(Rx)) in children with spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: This phase 1 study reports that a single intrathecal dose of nusinersen was well tolerated in children with type 2 or type 3 spinal muscular atrophy, increased CSF SMN protein at the 6- and 9-mg doses, and produced exploratory improvements in HFMSE motor-function scores, especially at 9 mg. The findings are preliminary because the study was open-label, single-dose, and small, and the efficacy results require confirmation in a controlled study.
papers.why: The phase 1 study provides human safety, pharmacokinetic, and preliminary functional efficacy data for intrathecal nusinersen in pediatric SMA.

papers.title: Pan-ethnic carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis for spinal muscular atrophy: clinical laboratory analysis of >72,400 specimens.
papers.summary: Large-scale clinical laboratory data show that SMN1 copy-number analysis is technically feasible for pan-ethnic SMA carrier screening and prenatal diagnosis, with a 91.2% pan-ethnic carrier detection rate and acceptable predictive performance. Performance and residual risk varied by ethnicity, and sequence variants in primer/probe-binding sites caused false-positive one-copy results that follow-up sequencing corrected.
papers.why: The study provides a validated high-throughput carrier-screening and prenatal-diagnosis workflow for SMA in more than 72,000 specimens.

papers.title: Spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes the genetic, cellular, and clinical mechanisms of spinal muscular atrophy and summarizes diagnostic, animal-model, pharmacological, gene-therapy, and stem-cell approaches reported in the literature. It reports that SMN1 loss is essential to pathogenesis, SMN2 copy number is primarily related to severity, exon 7 deletion testing is highly specific, and several experimental interventions improve SMN expression or disease phenotypes in cellular and mouse models, although no cure was available at the time of publication.
papers.why: The review provides a validated molecular diagnostic approach, genetic counseling and testing resources, and coordinated care recommendations applicable to SMA.

papers.title: Knockdown of the survival motor neuron (Smn) protein in zebrafish causes defects in motor axon outgrowth and pathfinding.
papers.summary: The study shows that reducing Smn protein in zebrafish embryos or individual motoneurons causes early, motoneuron-specific motor axon truncation and aberrant branching that are independent of motoneuron death. Human full-length SMN mRNA, but not hSMNΔ7 mRNA, partially rescues these defects, validating the system as an in vivo model of spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.why: This study develops and validates a zebrafish SMA model with measurable motor-axon outgrowth and pathfinding defects caused by Smn loss.

papers.title: Enhancement of SMN2 exon 7 inclusion by antisense oligonucleotides targeting the exon.
papers.summary: A positional antisense screen identified optimized 2′-O-methoxy-ethyl-modified antisense oligonucleotides, particularly ASO 07–21 and ASO 34–48, that increase inclusion of SMN2 exon 7 and raise full-length SMN mRNA, protein, and nuclear gem numbers in cultured SMA type I cells. The study provides a transferable two-step ASO-walk method for locating and optimizing exon-regulatory targets, but did not test clinical efficacy or rescue disease manifestations in animals or patients.
papers.why: Systematically identifies exon 7 inclusion-promoting SMN2 ASOs that increase full-length SMN protein in cell-free assays and cultured cells and can advance to mouse studies.

papers.title: Onasemnogene abeparvovec for presymptomatic infants with three copies of SMN2 at risk for spinal muscular atrophy: the Phase III SPR1NT trial.
papers.summary: In the Phase III single-arm SPR1NT trial, a single intravenous dose of onasemnogene abeparvovec given to 15 presymptomatic infants with biallelic SMN1 deletions and three SMN2 copies was associated with independently achieved standing in all children and walking in 14, while all remained alive without permanent ventilation and none required respiratory or feeding support. Treatment was generally well tolerated, although mild-to-moderate treatment-related hepatotoxicity and transient cardiac-enzyme elevations occurred.
papers.why: The Phase III SPR1NT study directly reports efficacy and tolerability of onasemnogene abeparvovec in presymptomatic infants at risk for SMA type 2.

papers.title: ISS-N1 makes the First FDA-approved Drug for Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes nusinersen (Spinraza) as the first FDA-approved therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, an antisense oligonucleotide that targets intronic splicing silencer N1 in SMN2 pre-mRNA to promote exon 7 inclusion and restore full-length SMN protein. It also identifies alternative RNA targets and delivery needs while noting that histone deacetylase inhibitors alone have not shown sufficient efficacy and that the effects of nusinersen on peripheral tissues remain uncertain.
papers.why: The paper describes the development and FDA approval of nusinersen as an antisense oligonucleotide correcting SMN2 exon 7 splicing in SMA.

papers.title: Evaluation of SMN protein, transcript, and copy number in the biomarkers for spinal muscular atrophy (BforSMA) clinical study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional cohort of 108 people with spinal muscular atrophy and 22 matched controls, blood-based SMN2 copy number and SMN transcript or protein levels distinguished SMA groups and related to clinical type, but no measure strongly predicted present motor function. The findings support blood SMN measurements as possible early target-engagement biomarkers for SMN-enhancing trials, while highlighting limited individual prognostic value, weak relationships among SMN measures, and imperfect representation of disease-relevant tissues by blood.
papers.why: The multicenter study evaluates blood-based SMN transcript, protein, and copy-number biomarkers alongside motor function for monitoring SMA and trial target engagement.

papers.title: A multi-source approach to determine SMA incidence and research ready population.
papers.summary: The study estimated the incidence of genetically confirmed spinal muscular atrophy in 18 European countries at 11.9 per 100,000 live births, corresponding to approximately 1 in 3,900–16,000 births. It also found that genetic laboratories, the TREAT-NMD Global SMA Patient Registry, and the Care and Trial Site Registry identify different subsets of patients, indicating that a portion of the SMA population remains inaccessible to specialist care and research opportunities.
papers.why: The study quantifies and demonstrates how SMA genetic-laboratory data, the global patient registry, and trial-site registry can support recruitment and SMA research.

papers.title: A transgene carrying an A2G missense mutation in the SMN gene modulates phenotypic severity in mice with severe (type I) spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that an SMN A2G missense transgene markedly modifies severe spinal muscular atrophy in SMN2;Smn−/− mice, producing a mild type III-like disease model when low levels of full-length SMN are present. The model exhibits delayed motor neuron loss, muscle atrophy, denervation, abnormal electromyography, and axonal degeneration, while the mutant SMN A2G protein alone cannot rescue embryonic lethality or efficiently self-associate and bind SmN.
papers.why: The engineered mild SMA mouse model enables in vivo study of SMN missense variants and testing of potential therapies.

papers.title: Motor function in type 2 and 3 SMA patients treated with Nusinersen: a critical review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This critical review and meta-analysis found consistent improvements in motor-function outcomes in real-world cohorts of people with type 2 or type 3 spinal muscular atrophy treated with Nusinersen, whereas reports from untreated cohorts generally described deterioration. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous cohorts, substantial statistical heterogeneity, small samples, inconsistent baseline reporting, and the absence of randomized or placebo-controlled comparisons in the included real-world studies.
papers.why: The meta-analysis provides evidence that nusinersen improves motor-function outcomes in type 2 and 3 SMA while identifying functional measures useful for evaluating treatment response.

papers.title: Clinical Trial and Postmarketing Safety of Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Therapy.
papers.summary: Across preclinical studies, seven clinical studies, and postmarketing reports, intravenous onasemnogene abeparvovec was associated with serious but generally monitorable and manageable safety risks in spinal muscular atrophy. The principal observed risks were hepatotoxicity, transient thrombocytopenia, cardiac events, thrombotic microangiopathy, and potential dorsal root ganglia toxicity, with no clinical evidence of ganglionopathy or sensory neuropathy.
papers.why: This study evaluates an approved SMA gene therapy across animal models, clinical trials, and postmarketing data and provides actionable safety monitoring and management findings.

papers.title: Specific inhibition of myostatin activation is beneficial in mouse models of SMA therapy.
papers.summary: The study shows that selective inhibition of myostatin activation with muSRK-015P improves skeletal muscle mass, force, and selected cortical and trabecular bone abnormalities in SMNΔ7 mice receiving early or later SMN restoration with SMN-C1. The findings support a complementary therapeutic strategy for residual muscle and bone deficits after SMN restoration, but the study did not test combination treatment with centrally administered nusinersen in patients or mice.
papers.why: The antibody improved muscle mass, function, and bone phenotypes in two SMN-restored mouse models of SMA, supporting myostatin inhibition as an adjunctive therapy.

papers.title: Cardiac pathology in spinal muscular atrophy: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review found 264 reported SMA cases with cardiac pathology and 14 studies of SMA mouse models, with structural defects concentrated in severe SMA type 1 and rhythm disorders more frequently reported in milder SMA types 2 and 3. The evidence suggests that SMN deficiency may affect cardiogenesis, cardiac autonomic development, and cardiac electrophysiology, but publication bias, absent control groups, inconsistent evaluation, and limited genetic confirmation prevent a definite conclusion that cardiac abnormalities are increased in SMA.
papers.why: This systematic review directly characterizes cardiac manifestations and disease models in SMA and identifies standardized cardiac outcome measures for SMA research.

papers.title: Two-year efficacy and safety of risdiplam in patients with type 2 or non-ambulant type 3 spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
papers.summary: In SUNFISH Part 2, risdiplam produced sustained improvement or stabilization of motor function over 24 months in children, teenagers, and adults with type 2 or non-ambulant type 3 spinal muscular atrophy. The treatment benefited MFM32, RULM, HFMSE, and caregiver-reported SMAIS-ULM outcomes, while forced vital capacity declined and no clinically significant new safety signal or risdiplam-associated toxicity was reported.
papers.why: This randomized phase III trial directly reports two-year efficacy, safety, and motor-function outcomes for approved splicing-modifier treatment in type 2 and non-ambulant type 3 SMA.

papers.title: Modeling the early phenotype at the neuromuscular junction of spinal muscular atrophy using patient-derived iPSCs.
papers.summary: The paper establishes an in vitro human iPSC-derived motor-neuron and myotube co-culture model of early spinal muscular atrophy neuromuscular-junction pathology, characterized by impaired acetylcholine receptor clustering and neurofilament accumulation without motor-neuron loss. Valproic acid and an SMN2-targeting phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligonucleotide improved receptor clustering; valproic acid increased full-length SMN transcripts but did not rescue neurofilament accumulation, whereas the morpholino also partially improved neurofilament accumulation.
papers.why: Creates an SMA patient-specific iPSC neuromuscular-junction model and shows that two tested treatments improve AChR clustering while increasing full-length SMN transcripts.

papers.title: Combined deficiency of Senataxin and DNA-PKcs causes DNA damage accumulation and neurodegeneration in spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: The paper finds that chronic SMN deficiency is associated with combined Senataxin (SETX) and DNA-PKcs deficiency, leading to RNA–DNA hybrid accumulation, DNA double-strand breaks, genomic instability, and neurodegeneration in SMA. Restoring SMN or increasing SETX rescues DNA-damage phenotypes in patient cells or SMA mouse neurons, identifying SETX as a candidate therapeutic target.
papers.why: Shows in SMA patient cells, mice, and spinal cord tissue that SMN loss causes SETX/DNA-PKcs deficiency and DNA damage, while SETX overexpression reduces damage and rescues neurodegeneration.

papers.title: European ad-hoc consensus statement on gene replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: This European consensus statement finds that onasemnogene abeparvovec is an approved gene replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, but supporting evidence is concentrated in infants with early-stage disease. It recommends individualized risk-benefit assessment, early treatment, expert treatment centres, standardized long-term monitoring, and particular caution for older, heavier, or advanced-disease patients in whom safety and efficacy remain uncertain.
papers.why: Provides disease-specific consensus guidance for selecting, administering, and monitoring onasemnogene abeparvovec in patients with SMA.

papers.title: Onasemnogene abeparvovec in spinal muscular atrophy: an Australian experience of safety and efficacy.
papers.summary: In a prospective Australian cohort of 21 infants with spinal muscular atrophy, onasemnogene abeparvovec was associated with motor gains and stabilization or improvement of respiratory or bulbar function, but caused frequent transient vomiting, transaminitis, thrombocytopaenia, and two cases of thrombotic microangiopathy after prior nusinersen. The study also identifies body weight, sequential treatment, and intensive laboratory surveillance as important considerations for treatment selection and safety monitoring.
papers.why: Provides real-world safety and efficacy data for onasemnogene abeparvovec in infants with SMA, including motor, feeding, respiratory, and laboratory monitoring outcomes.

papers.title: Development of a single vector system that enhances trans-splicing of SMN2 transcripts.
papers.summary: The study shows that a single plasmid, pMU3, co-expressing an SMN trans-splicing RNA and the ASO In711 that blocks the SMN2 intron 7/exon 8 splice site, enhances production of functional full-length SMN. The strategy increased SMN protein and SMN-containing nuclear gems in primary SMA fibroblasts and raised SMN protein and U11ATAC snRNP assembly activity; intracerebroventricular delivery also increased spinal-cord SMN in SMNΔ7 mice.
papers.why: Reports an optimized gene-therapy strategy that increases full-length SMN in patient fibroblasts, the CNS of SMA mice, and an in vitro snRNP assay.

papers.title: The First Orally Deliverable Small Molecule for the Treatment of Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes the molecular basis of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and compares approved and investigational splicing-directed therapies. It highlights risdiplam as an orally deliverable small molecule that increases SMN2 exon 7 inclusion and SMN expression, improves motor and survival outcomes in mouse models, and produced functional or survival benefits in clinical trials, while noting off-target splicing and adverse events as limitations.
papers.why: The paper identifies risdiplam as an approved oral small-molecule therapy and compares it with established antisense and gene-therapy solutions for SMA.

papers.title: Myostatin inhibition in combination with antisense oligonucleotide therapy improves outcomes in spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: In severe Taiwanese spinal muscular atrophy mice, systemic AAV-mediated myostatin propeptide expression enhanced several effects of the SMN2-splicing antisense oligomer PMO25, including body weight, muscle mass, fibre size, neuromuscular-junction maturation, sensory-neuron size, proprioceptive synapses, and selected functional outcomes. Benefits depended on disease severity and PMO25 dose: myostatin inhibition alone was modest, high-dose PMO25 combination therapy did not improve survival, and low-dose PMO25 combination therapy significantly prolonged survival without increasing motor-neuron number.
papers.why: Shows that PMO25 combined with AAV-mediated myostatin blockade improves survival, muscle mass, neuromuscular maturation, motor function, and exercise performance in severe SMA mice.

papers.title: Total protein analysis as a reliable loading control for quantitative fluorescent Western blotting.
papers.summary: In spinal cord tissue from a severe mouse model of spinal muscular atrophy, quantitative fluorescent Western blotting showed reduced β-actin and β-tubulin expression compared with littermate controls, whereas total protein load was nearly unchanged. The study proposes total protein analysis, performed in parallel with Coomassie staining, as a more reliable normalization method than single-protein loading controls.
papers.why: Demonstrates and validates a Western-blot loading-control method that corrects artifacts in quantitative protein studies, including an SMA spinal-cord model.

papers.title: Temporal and tissue-specific variability of SMN protein levels in mouse models of spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: This study quantifies tissue- and age-dependent survival motor neuron (SMN) protein depletion in severe Taiwanese and intermediate Smn2B/− mouse models of spinal muscular atrophy. It shows that baseline SMN expression varies markedly across tissues and developmental stages, while the severity and tissue pattern of depletion differ substantially between the two models.
papers.why: The work directly characterizes two established SMA mouse models and quantifies tissue- and time-dependent SMN depletion to inform therapeutic requirements and translational endpoints.

papers.title: Real-World Outcomes in Patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy Treated with Onasemnogene Abeparvovec Monotherapy: Findings from the RESTORE Registry.
papers.summary: The RESTORE registry provides real-world observational evidence for onasemnogene abeparvovec monotherapy in 168 patients with spinal muscular atrophy. Treatment was associated with improved event-free survival, motor function, motor-milestone attainment, and oral feeding, while treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events were reported and were generally consistent with the established safety profile.
papers.why: Reports real-world effectiveness, motor outcomes, milestone attainment, and safety data for gene-replacement therapy in 168 patients with SMA.

papers.title: Longitudinal natural history of type I spinal muscular atrophy: a critical review.
papers.summary: This review merged longitudinal untreated natural-history data from 38 infants with genetically confirmed type I spinal muscular atrophy and found no sustained improvement in CHOP INTEND scores; motor function consistently declined, with trajectories varying by age, baseline score, and SMN2 copy number. The resulting dataset and CHOP INTEND baseline scores provide reference trajectories for interpreting treatment responses in clinical trials and real-world studies.
papers.why: The cumulative natural-history analysis provides validated CHOP INTEND trajectories and prognostic strata for untreated type I SMA.

papers.title: ZPR1 prevents R-loop accumulation, upregulates SMN2 expression and rescues spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: The study shows that ZPR1 overexpression increases SMN2 transcription and SMN protein, restores SETX and DNA-PKcs, reduces R-loop accumulation and DNA damage, and partially rescues disease phenotypes in SMAΔ7 mice and patient-derived cells. ZPR1 is therefore proposed as an SMN-dependent protective modifier and therapeutic target, but efficacy and safety of pharmacological or AAV9-mediated ZPR1 upregulation remain untested in humans.
papers.why: ZPR1 overexpression directly increases SMN2 and SMN levels and rescues motor, growth, lifespan, neuronal, R-loop, and DNA-damage phenotypes in SMA mice and patient cells.

papers.title: Intrathecal Onasemnogene Abeparvovec for Sitting, Nonambulatory Patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy: Phase I Ascending-Dose Study (STRONG).
papers.summary: In the phase I STRONG trial, a single intrathecal dose of onasemnogene abeparvovec was generally safe and produced clinically meaningful motor-function improvement in treated children aged 24 to <60 months with SMA and three SMN2 copies. Independent standing and walking were not significantly improved in the younger cohort, and treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in every patient, including isolated serious transaminase elevations and transient thrombocytopenia.
papers.why: The phase I STRONG study directly tested intrathecal gene therapy in sitting, nonambulatory SMA patients and reported safety, motor benefit, vector-genome measures, and HFMSE outcomes.

papers.title: Upper limb evaluation and one-year follow up of non-ambulant patients with spinal muscular atrophy: an observational multicenter trial.
papers.summary: This observational multicenter study found that MyoGrip, MyoPinch, and MoviPlate, together with the Motor Function Measure, were feasible and highly reliable for assessing upper-limb function in non-ambulant patients with SMA types II and III. Distal strength increased in patients younger than 14 years and generally deteriorated in patients older than 14 years, while MoviPlate showed a learning effect and MFM did not significantly change over 12 months.
papers.why: This multicenter longitudinal SMA study validates sensitive upper-limb functional devices and clinical scales as outcome measures for clinical trials.

papers.title: Diverse targets of SMN2-directed splicing-modulating small molecule therapeutics for spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: Risdiplam and branaplam restored SMN2 exon 7 inclusion in type I SMA patient fibroblasts, but high concentrations caused extensive, compound-specific changes in gene expression and pre-mRNA splicing. Minigene and sequence-mutational experiments identified context-dependent cis-elements, and combined low-dose treatment retained or improved SMN2 exon 7 restoration while showing fewer off-target effects than high-dose single treatment.
papers.why: The study directly compares risdiplam and branaplam in SMA patient cells, quantifies their off-target splicing effects, and demonstrates benefits of low-dose combination treatment.

papers.title: Specificity, synergy, and mechanisms of splice-modifying drugs.
papers.summary: The study shows that risdiplam and branaplam increase inclusion of SMN2 exon 7 by targeting the U1 snRNP–5′ splice-site complex, with quantitative models supporting one sequence-specific interaction mode for risdiplam and two for branaplam. It also contradicts the prevailing two-site mechanism for risdiplam and finds widespread anomalous single-drug cooperativity and multi-drug synergy among splice-modifying treatments, although risdiplam and branaplam do not significantly synergize with each other.
papers.why: The study provides experimental and quantitative data on the mechanisms, specificity, and synergy of the SMA splice-modifying drugs risdiplam and branaplam, along with transferable methods for evaluating splice-modifying therapies.

papers.title: Restoring SMN Expression: An Overview of the Therapeutic Developments for the Treatment of Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: This review describes how spinal muscular atrophy results from deficient SMN protein and summarizes therapeutic strategies that restore SMN1 expression or modify SMN2 splicing. Nusinersen, onasemnogene abeparvovec, and risdiplam have demonstrated clinical benefit, although delivery limitations, incomplete respiratory recovery, adverse events, and potential long-term SMN overexpression toxicity remain important constraints.
papers.why: The paper summarizes three clinically validated disease-modifying approaches for SMA that directly restore or increase functional SMN expression.

papers.title: SMA-causing missense mutations in survival motor neuron (Smn) display a wide range of phenotypes when modeled in Drosophila.
papers.summary: The paper generated twelve patient-derived Drosophila Smn missense alleles and showed that they reproduce a broad range of SMA-like phenotypic severities, with severity associated with defects in SMN self-oligomerization and interactions with Gemin proteins. Overexpression of wild-type Drosophila SMN substantially rescued the dominant-negative viability defect of the severe SmnY203C allele, supporting restoration of functional SMN oligomers as a potential therapeutic strategy for severe SMN1 point mutations.
papers.why: The study directly models human SMA-causing SMN1 variants in Drosophila and provides experimentally validated phenotypic, genetic, biochemical, and structural assays of mutant SMN activity.

papers.title: Gene therapy rescues disease phenotype in a spinal muscular atrophy with respiratory distress type 1 (SMARD1) mouse model.
papers.summary: Systemic, single-dose AAV9-IGHMBP2 gene therapy substantially rescued motor-neuron degeneration, neuromuscular abnormalities, muscle pathology, motor dysfunction, and mortality in the nmd mouse model of SMARD1, while genetic correction with wild-type IGHMBP2 protected human SMARD1 iPSC-derived motor neurons in culture. The study provides preclinical proof of principle for IGHMBP2 replacement and explicitly identifies mechanistic and therapeutic similarities with spinal muscular atrophy linked to chromosome 5q.
papers.why: The paper directly demonstrates rescue of SMARD1, an IGHMBP2-associated spinal muscular atrophy subtype, using AAV9 gene replacement in mice and patient-derived motor neurons.

papers.title: Overview of Current Drugs and Molecules in Development for Spinal Muscular Atrophy Therapy.
papers.summary: This review concludes that approved nusinersen and developing SMN-restoring therapies improve important outcomes in spinal muscular atrophy, although efficacy is incomplete, phenotype-dependent, and influenced by treatment timing. It also identifies SMN-independent and combination strategies targeting neuroprotection, muscle function, actin dynamics, endocytosis, ubiquitin homeostasis, and ribosome biology, while highlighting null results for valproic acid and major translational limitations.
papers.why: This review summarizes disease-modifying and investigational therapies tested or developed for spinal muscular atrophy, including SMN-restoring and SMN-independent approaches.

papers.title: Increasing Agrin Function Antagonizes Muscle Atrophy and Motor Impairment in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: Daily subcutaneous NT-1654 from birth in SMAΔ7 mice improved selected motor behaviors, preserved muscle-fiber size, reduced neurofilament accumulation, and modestly extended survival. Some NMJ and motor effects were incomplete or statistically nonsignificant, and NT-1654 produced only a nonsignificant trend toward increased lumbar motor-neuron survival.
papers.why: The study directly tests NT-1654 in an SMA mouse model and reports improved neuromuscular-junction maturation, muscle preservation, motor function, and survival.

papers.title: Therapy development for spinal muscular atrophy: perspectives for muscular dystrophies and neurodegenerative disorders.
papers.summary: This review describes how therapies for spinal muscular atrophy restore deficient Survival Motor Neuron protein through SMN2 exon 7 inclusion or SMN1 gene transfer. Clinical evidence supports Nusinersen, Risdiplam, and Onasemnogene abeparvovec, while additional approaches target motoneurons, neuromuscular junctions, muscle, and modifier pathways, with important limitations in timing, delivery, and toxicity.
papers.why: The review consolidates validated SMA therapies, model systems, and translational methods that can accelerate research in SMA and related neuromuscular degenerations.

papers.title: Recombinant Adeno-Associated Virus Serotype 9 Gene Therapy in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
papers.summary: This review finds that onasemnogene abeparvovec, an AAV9-mediated SMN1 gene-replacement therapy, improves motor and respiratory outcomes in many infants with spinal muscular atrophy, with greater benefit when administered earlier. It also reports important treatment-related hepatic, cardiac, hematologic, renal, and thrombotic adverse events, including acute liver injury and thrombotic microangiopathy, and emphasizes that long-term efficacy and safety remain uncertain.
papers.why: Reports clinical-trial efficacy and real-world safety of approved AAV9 SMN1 gene replacement and summarizes other established disease-modifying SMA therapies.

papers.title: Treatment expectations and patient-reported outcomes of nusinersen therapy in adult spinal muscular atrophy.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal observational study of 24 adults with SMA types 2–4, nusinersen was associated with patient-reported improvements in muscle strength, endurance, independence, and modest increases in HFMSE and RULM scores over approximately 10–18 months. Some patients experienced worsening, and the authors could not draw definitive efficacy conclusions because the cohort was small, lacked an untreated control, and used an unvalidated symptom questionnaire.
papers.why: The longitudinal adult SMA study provides outcome-measure data and real-world evidence of modest functional and patient-reported benefit from nusinersen.

papers.title: The Effect of a Muscle-mimicking, Fabric-type Shoulder Orthosis on Functional Movements of the Upper Limb in Patients With Neuromuscular Disorder
papers.summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to investigate the effect of a muscle-mimicking, fabric-type shoulder orthosis on functional movements of the upper limb in patients with neuromuscular disorder.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the impact of the muscle-mimicking, fabric-type shoulder orthosis on upper limb functional movements in patients with neuromuscular disorder?
* Are there observable differences in upper limb function when the shoulder orthosis is worn versus when it is not?

Participants will:

* Receive education on how to wear and use the shoulder orthosis.

papers.title: Efficacy and Usability of the EXPLORER Exoskeleton in Children With Neurodevelopmental Disorders in Natural Environments
papers.summary:
Neurodevelopmental disorders often lead to abnormal development of the Central Nervous System (CNS), frequently causing motor dysfunctions such as an inability to stand and walk. EXPLORER is a robotic gait exoskeleton designed to rehabilitate children with motor disabilities in home and outdoor environments.

The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and usability of EXPLORER in children with motor disability within their natural settings, including home and community environments.

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics and Efficacy of Risdiplam (RO7034067) in Type 2 and 3 Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Participants
papers.summary: Multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of Risdiplam in adult and pediatric participants with Type 2 and Type 3 SMA. The study consists of two parts, an exploratory dose finding part (Part 1) of Risdiplam for 12 weeks and a confirmatory part (Part 2) of Risdiplam for 24 months.

papers.title: Spinal Muscular Atrophy on Wheels, Using Power Mobility
papers.summary:
The group of children diagnosed with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) has serious restrictions on participation. SMA is a neuromuscular disease that leads to neuromusculoskeletal disorders that limit functional activities, sometimes making it impossible to sit down autonomously and to walk.

papers.title: A Study of RO6885247 in Adult and Pediatric Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (MOONFISH)
papers.summary: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, 12-week, placebo-controlled multiple dose study will investigate the safety and tolerability of RO6885247 in adult and pediatric patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

papers.title: Study of Safety and Dosing Effect on SMN Levels of Valproic Acid (VPA) in Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This is an open label phase I/II clinical trial to assess safety, tolerability and potential effect on SMN mRNA and protein in vivo of a compound in which preliminary evidence supports a potential effect on SMN levels in vitro.

papers.title: Pre-Symptomatic Study of Intravenous Onasemnogene Abeparvovec-xioi in Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) for Patients With Multiple Copies of SMN2
papers.summary: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of intravenous onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi in pre-symptomatic patients with SMA and 2 or 3 copies SMN2

papers.title: Exoskeleton Impact on the Quality of Life on Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of the use of a pediatric exoskeleton on the quality of life of children, specifically in the psychological and care dimensions. Other objectives are to evaluate changes at the physical and functional level.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Apitegromab in Patients With Later-Onset Spinal Muscular Atrophy Treated With Nusinersen or Risdiplam
papers.summary: This Phase 3 trial (Study SRK-015-003) was conducted in patients ≥2 years old at Screening, who were previously diagnosed with later-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) (i.e., Type 2 and Type 3 SMA) and were receiving an approved survival motor neuron (SMN) upregulator therapy (i.e., either nusinersen or risdiplam), to confirm the efficacy and safety of apitegromab as an adjunctive therapy to nusinersen and evaluate the efficacy and safety of apitegromab as an adjunctive therapy to risdiplam.

papers.title: Study of the Safety and Efficacy of an Adeno-Associated Viral Vector Carrying the SMN Gene After a Single Intravenous Administration of Escalating Doses in Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (BLUEBELL)
papers.summary: The goal of this multicenter, open-label, non-comparative, cohort study is to investigate the safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy of ANB-004 in children with spinal muscular atrophy. The study will have a standard 3+3 dose-escalation design.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Safety and Tolerability of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA).
papers.summary: The primary objective of Part 1 of this study is to assess the safety and tolerability of Nusinersen in participants with SMA who are not eligible to participate in the clinical studies ISIS 396443-CS3B (NCT02193074) or ISIS 396443-CS4 (NCT02292537). The secondary objective of Part 1 of this study is to examine the pharmacokinetics (PK) of Nusinersen in participants with SMA. The primary objective of Part 2 of this study is to assess the long-term safety and tolerability of Nusinersen in participants with SMA who participated in Part 1 and completed their End of Part 1 Evaluation assessments.

papers.title: Study to Evaluate Sodium Phenylbutyrate in Pre-symptomatic Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: In this single-center trial, we will evaluate the effects of NaPB on presymptomatic Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) type I (cohort 1)and presymptomatic SMA type II (cohort 2) infants. A variety of outcome measures will be performed at each study visit to follow the course of the disease. Total duration of the study for type I infants will be 18 months, for type II infants, 24 months.

papers.title: Safety, Usability, and Effectiveness of a Gait Exoskeleton for Children and Adolescents With Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
papers.summary: Neurodevelopmental disorders often result in abnormal development of the Central Nervous System (CNS), frequently causing motor dysfunctions such as the inability to stand and walk. CLINICAL EXPLORER is a clinical-use robotic device for gait training, representing the evolution of the ATLAS 2030 exoskeleton and the EXPLORER device for home use. The aim of this study is to evaluate the safety and usability of CLINICAL EXPLORER .

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Intrathecal OAV101 (AVXS-101) in Pediatric Patients With Type 2 Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)
papers.summary: This was a Phase III multi-center, single dose (1.2 x 10\^14 vector genomes), randomized, sham controlled, double-blind study that investigates the efficacy, safety and tolerability of OAV101B in treatment naive, sitting and never ambulatory SMA patients 2 to \<18 years of age.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy Evaluation of GC101 Gene Therapy Via Intrathecal (IT) Injectionin the Treatment of Patients With Type 2 Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) - Phase III
papers.summary: This trial employs a multicenter, randomized, open-label, standard-of-care-controlled design and plans to enroll 50 patients with Type 2 SMA aged 2 to 12 years who have previously received nusinersen. The primary objective of the trial is to evaluate the efficacy of GC101 in treating Type 2 SMA. The secondary objectives are to assess the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of GC101 in treating Type 2 SMA.

papers.title: A Study of Risdiplam (RO7034067) in Adult and Pediatric Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This is a multi-center, exploratory, non-comparative, and open-label study to investigate the safety, tolerability, PK, and PK/PD relationship of risdiplam in adults, children and infants with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) previously enrolled in Study BP29420 (Moonfish) with the splicing modifier RO6885247 or previously treated with nusinersen, olesoxime or AVXS-101.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted vs Landmark Based Intrathecal Administration of Nusinersen
papers.summary:
Intrathecal administration of Nusinersen, an antisense oligonucleotide capable of increasing Survival Motor Neuron protein production, has been tested in Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) to improve motor function and survival. A feature of adult SMA patients is a progressive neuromyopathic scoliosis, so spinal nusinersen administration can be challenging. Landmark identification using a pre-procedure ultrasound (US) facilitates technical performance of spinal anesthesia and allows for the elimination of radiation exposure.

papers.title: NuroSleeve Powered Brace & Stimulation System to Restore Arm Function
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate if a person with weakness or paralysis in one or both arms, can use the NuroSleeve combined powered arm brace (orthosis) and muscle stimulation system to help restore movement in one arm sufficient to perform daily activities. This study could lead to the development of a product that could allow people with arm weakness or arm paralysis to use the NuroSleeve and similar devices to improve arm health and independent function.

papers.title: Phase II Study of Leuprolide and Testosterone for Men With Kennedy's Disease or Other Motor Neuron Disease
papers.summary:
OBJECTIVES:

I. Evaluate the effects of androgen suppression with leuprolide and androgen replacement with testosterone enanthate on muscle strength in men with Kennedy's disease or other motor neuron disease.

papers.title: Levetiracetam for Cramps, Spasticity and Neuroprotection in Motor Neuron Disease
papers.summary: Levetiracetam (Keppra) is used to treat partial onset seizures. Its biological effects suggest it might also be useful in treating 3 aspects of human motor neuron diseases (MNDs) for which no effective therapy exists: cramps, spasticity, and disease progression.

papers.title: Clinical Trial of Sodium Phenylbutyrate in Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Types II or III
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to identify the maximum tolerated dosage of sodium phenylbutyrate in children with spinal muscular atrophy types II or III; and to determine if the drug has an effect on SMN mRNA and protein levels.

papers.title: Clinical Trial to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of EXG001-307 in Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this trial is to evaluate safety and efficacy of intrathecal delivery of EXG001-307 as a treatment of spinal muscular atrophy .

papers.title: A Pilot Therapeutic Trial Using Hydroxyurea in Type I Spinal Muscular Atrophy Patients
papers.summary: The objectives of this trial are: to establish a safety profile for use of Hydroxyurea in children with Type I Spinal Muscular Atrophy; to identify reliable outcome measures for HU treatment in Type I SMA; and to detect the clinical efficacy of HU treatment in children with Type I SMA.

papers.title: A Study to Learn About the Effect of Nusinersen (BIIB058) Given as Injections to Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Who Were Previously Treated With Onasemnogene Abeparvovec (RESPOND)
papers.summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about the use of nusinersen (BIIB058) in participants with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). This study will focus on children under the age of 3 who were previously treated with the gene therapy onasemnogene abeparvovec but are still facing health challenges related to their disease.

The main goal of the study is to learn about the effect nusinersen has on muscle and movement ability (motor function). The main question researchers want to answer is:

papers.title: Whole Body Vibration Therapy in Children With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) are one of the common physical disabilities in childhood. For SMA, progressive muscle weakness and early fatigue hamper the mobility of the sufferers. Osteopenia is common for this population group due to poor bone growth and muscle disuse. As a result, non-traumatic related fractures and bone pain are common. Recently, whole body vibration therapy (WBVT) has been proven to improve bone health and muscle function in healthy adults and post-menopausal women. papers.title: Valproic Acid and Carnitine in Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This is a multi-center trial to assess safety and efficacy of a combined regimen of oral valproic acid (VPA) and carnitine in patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) 2 to 17 years of age. Cohort 1 is a double-blind placebo-controlled randomized intention to treat protocol for SMA "sitters" 2 - 8 years of age. Cohort 2 is an open label protocol for SMA "standers and walkers" 3 - 17 years of age to explore responsiveness of efficacy outcomes. Outcome measures will include blood chemistries, functional testing, pulmonary function testing, electrophysiological evaluations, PedsQL quality of li

papers.title: A Study of CK-2127107 in Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This study will evaluate the pharmacodynamic (PD) effect of CK-2127107 (hereafter referred to as reldesemtiv) versus placebo on measures of skeletal muscle function or fatigability in patients with Type II, III, or IV spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: The primary objective of the study is to examine the clinical efficacy of nusinersen (ISIS 396443) administered intrathecally (IT) to participants with infantile-onset with infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). The secondary objective of the study is to examine the safety and tolerability of nusinersen administered intrathecally to participants with infantile-onset SMA.

papers.title: A Study to Learn About the Effect of Higher Doses of Nusinersen (BIIB058) Given as Injections to Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Who Were Previously Treated With Risdiplam (ASCEND)
papers.summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about the use of a higher dose of nusinersen (BIIB058) in participants with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). This study will focus on teenagers and adults who are unable to walk on their own and who have previously taken another drug for SMA called risdiplam.

The main goal of this study is to learn about the effect of high dose (HD) nusinersen on muscle and movement ability (motor function) in SMA. The main question that researchers want to answer is:

\- How do the scores of a movement test called the Revised Upper Limb Module change from the start of

papers.title: A Study of the Safety and Preliminary Efficacy of NKG001 in Pediatric Patients With Type 1 or Type 2 Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary:
This study is a single-center, open-label, single-arm, non-randomized, single-dose, dose-escalation investigator-initiated trial (IIT) designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of NKG001 Injection administered via different dosing regimens (intravenous \[IV\] alone or intravenous combined with intrathecal \[IV+IT\]) in subjects with Type 1 or Type 2 spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

A total of 13-21 SMA subjects aged ≤60 months are planned to be enrolled. Based on age at enrollment, subjects will be stratified into two age cohorts for independent evaluation:
