papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Risdiplam (RO7034067) Given by Mouth in Healthy Volunteers
papers.summary: The objective of this study is to assess the safety and tolerability of Risdiplam (RO7034067) in healthy people. The study will assess what the body does to Risdiplam (RO7034067) and what Risdiplam (RO7034067) does to the body. Risdiplam (RO7034067) will be given by mouth in gradually increasing doses. The data from this study will help to define the dose to further explore Risdiplam (RO7034067) in patients with Spinal Muscular Atrophy.

papers.title: A Study to Learn About the Long-Term Safety of Higher Doses of Nusinersen (BIIB058) Given as Injections to Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Who Took Part in an Earlier Nusinersen Trial (ONWARD)
papers.summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about the use of nusinersen (BIIB058) in participants with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). This study is an extension study and will enroll only those participants who have completed treatment in the parent study, 232SM203.

The main goal of the study is to learn about the long-term safety of nusinersen. The main questions researchers want to answer are:

* How many participants have adverse events and serious adverse events during the study?
* How do the results of electrocardiograms (ECGs), vital signs, and laboratory tests including blood and urine

papers.title: A Drug-drug Interaction Study With Risdiplam Multiple Dose and Midazolam in Healthy Participants
papers.summary: This will be a Phase I, 2-part, open-label, non-randomized study to investigate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of a multiple-dosing regimen of risdiplam (Part 1) and the effect of risdiplam on the PK of midazolam (Part 2) following oral administration in healthy adult male and female participants.

papers.title: Flu Vaccine Study in Neuromuscular Patients 2011
papers.summary: The purpose of the study is to compare the immune response of two different injection methods (Intramuscular V.S. Subcutaneous) of the 2011-2012 seasonal Influenza (Flu) vaccine among patients with neuromuscular conditions who have significant muscle degeneration. This research study hypothesizes that the subcutaneous route of vaccine administration, as compared to the intramuscular route, may confer at least comparable, or possibly better, immunogenicity. At least 30 individuals followed by the CCHMC Neuromuscular Comprehensive Care Center will be recruited to participate in this study lastin

papers.title: Controlled Trial to Evaluate Amifampridine Phosphate in Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 3 Patients
papers.summary: A two-period, two-treatment, crossover study to evaluate the safety, tolerability and efficacy of amifampridine phosphate in ambulatory patients diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) Type 3.

papers.title: SWITCH II Early Feasibility Study: Implantable BCI to Control a Digital Device for People With Paralysis
papers.summary:
The Synchron Motor Neuroprosthesis (MNP) is intended to be used in subjects with severe motor impairment, unresponsive to medical or rehabilitative therapy and a persistent functioning motor cortex. The purpose of this research is to evaluate safety and feasibility.

The MNP is a type of implantable brain computer interface which bypasses dysfunctional motor neurons. The device is designed to restore the transmission of neural signal from the cerebral cortex utilized for neuromuscular control of digital devices, resulting in a successful execution of non-mechanical digital commands.

papers.title: Real World Clinical Effectiveness & Safety of Vesemnogene Lantuparvovec for Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) in Low-middle Income Countries (LMIC).
papers.summary:
The study objective is to determine the real-world safety and effectiveness of Vesemnogene lantuparvovec for the treatment of SMA.

The specific objectives are:

* To determine clinical effectiveness of Vesemnogene lantuparvovec therapy for SMA as evaluated by developmental gross motor milestone and survival.
* To describe the safety profile of Vesemnogene therapy for SMA as evaluated by adverse events reporting and laboratory tests, and monitoring of Adverse events of special interest.

papers.title: Bioavailability and Bioequivalence of Two Risdiplam Tablets in Healthy Participants
papers.summary: The study is a randomized, single oral dose, crossover study in up to three parts to investigate the relative bioavailability and bioequivalence of two different formulations of risdiplam 5 mg (dispersible tablets) versus the current risdiplam oral solution formulation in healthy male and female participants. The effect of food on these two dispersible tablets and the current oral solution will be studied, as well as the effect of omeprazole on the dispersible tablets.

papers.title: An Open Label Study of Gene Therapy Product (Vesemnogene Lantuparvovec) in Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This is an interventional study to evaluate safety and efficacy of AAV-hSMN1 in spinal muscular atrophy patients.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)
papers.summary: The primary objective is to examine the clinical efficacy of multiple doses of nusinersen (ISIS 396443) administered intrathecally to participants with Infantile-Onset Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA). The secondary objectives are to examine the safety and tolerability of multiple doses of nusinersen administered intrathecally to participants with infantile-onset SMA and to examine the cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) and plasma Pharmacokinetics (PK) of multiple doses of nusinersen administered intrathecally to participants with infantile-onset SMA.

papers.title: CARNIVAL Type I: Valproic Acid and Carnitine in Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Type I
papers.summary: This is a multi-center trial to test safety and evaluate early treatment intervention with valproic acid and carnitine in moderating SMA symptoms of Type I infants.

papers.title: An Open-label Safety, Tolerability and Dose-Range Finding Study of Multiple Doses of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary:
This study will test the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of escalating doses of nusinersen (ISIS 396443) administered into the spinal fluid either two or three times over the duration of the trial, in participants with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

Four dose levels will be evaluated sequentially. Each dose level will be studied in a cohort of approximately 8 participants, where all participants will receive active drug.

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy of NMD670 in Ambulatory Adult Patients With Type 3 Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy, safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics of NMD670 in the treatment of ambulatory adults with spinal muscular atrophy type 3

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Efficacy, Pharmacokinetics, and Immunogenicity of Intravenous Administration of ARGX-119 in Pediatric Participants Aged 5 to Less Than 18 Years With Spinal Muscular Atrophy
papers.summary: This study aims to find the correct dose of ARGX-119 for children with SMA. The study will also look at how safe the study drug is, how well it works, how it moves through the body, and how the immune system responds to it. The study consists of a double-blinded treatment period (DBTP) where participants will either receive ARGX-119 IV or placebo IV, in addition to disease-modifying therapy (DMT) for 24 weeks. Participants who complete the DBTP will enter the open-label active-treatment extension period (ATEP) during which all participants will receive ARGX-119 IV up to 100 weeks (approximatel

papers.title: An Open-label Safety and Tolerability Study of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Who Previously Participated in ISIS 396443-CS1 (NCT01494701)
papers.summary: The primary objective of this study is to examine the safety and tolerability of nusinersen (ISIS 396443) administered intrathecally to participants with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) who previously participated in ISIS 396443-CS1 (NCT02865109). The secondary objective was to examine the plasma pharmacokinetics of a single dose of ISIS 396443 administered intrathecally to participants with SMA who previously participated in ISIS 396443-CS1.

papers.title: An Open-label Safety, Tolerability, and Dose-range Finding Study of Nusinersen (ISIS 396443) in Participants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)
papers.summary: This objectives of this study are to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of a single dose of nusinersen (ISIS 396443) administered intrathecally to participants with Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA).

papers.title: A Pilot Therapeutic Trial Using Hydroxyurea in Type II and Type III Spinal Muscular Atrophy Patients
papers.summary: The objectives of this trial are: to establish a safety profile for use of Hydroxyurea in children with Types II and III Spinal Muscular Atrophy; to identify reliable outcome measures for HU treatment in Types II and III SMA; and to detect the clinical efficacy of HU treatment in children with Types II and III SMA.

papers.title: Schulze Muscular Dystrophy Ability Clinical Study
papers.summary: The primary objective of the Schulze study is to evaluate the function of the upper limbs of subjects diagnosed with neuromuscular disorders, with and without use of the Abilitech Assist device in the clinic and home environments. Functional outcomes will include documenting active range of motion and the ability to perform activities of daily living (ADLs) using the standardized Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM) and the Role Evaluation of Activities of Life (REAL) assessments. Secondary objectives are to assess the safety record and report on adverse events (AEs) and parameters

papers.title: Short and Long Term Treatment With 4-AP in Ambulatory SMA Patients
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to assess whether 4-AP (Dalfampridine-ER, Ampyra) improves walking ability and endurance in adult patients with Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) Type 3 compared to placebo and whether the duration of treatment affects outcome.

papers.title: Evaluation of Safety and Efficacy of Gene Therapy Drug in the Treatment of Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Type 3 Patients
papers.summary: The study will evaluate safety and efficacy of intrathecal delivery of GC101 gene therapy drug as a treatment of spinal muscular atrophy Type 3 (SMA 3) patients.

papers.title: Trial Evaluating the Interest of Noninvasive Ventilation in NAVA Mode in Respiratory Decompensations Children With Infantile Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type II
papers.summary:
The new NAVA® ventilatory mode with the SERVO-i ventilator (Maquet®) uses the electrical activity of the diaphragm (EADi) as a marker for triggering the respiratory cycle. The EADi is captured by the electrodes of a specific catheter (the Edi® catheter) placed in the esophagus as a regular gastric feeding tube, and relayed to the SERVO-i who displays it and delivers respiratory assistance according to measured Edi signal which allows synchronous assistance, proportional to the respiratory efforts of the patient.

To date, no measure of the effectiveness of NAVA NAV has been performed in childr

papers.title: Safety and Efficacy Study of Pyridostigmine on Patients With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 3
papers.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate safety and efficacy of anti-cholinesterase therapy on the motor function in SMA type 3 patients with impaired neuromuscular junction (NMJ).

papers.title: A Phase I/II Clinical Study to Evaluate SKG0201 Injection in Subjects With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type I
papers.summary: This is a phase I/II clinical study to evaluate the safety, preliminary efficacy and immunogenicity of SKG0201 injection in subjects with Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type I.

papers.title: Study of Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of GB221 in Infants With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 1
papers.summary:
GB221 is a gene therapy that delivers a working SMN1 gene to the motor neurons of people with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) Type 1. This study will evaluate the safety, tolerability and efficacy of GB221 in two groups:

1. participants aged from 2 weeks to younger than 12 months presenting with symptoms of SMA Type 1 who have never received a treatment OR are receiving the drug risdiplam
2. participants aged from 2 weeks to younger than 5 months who are at risk of developing SMA Type 1 (presymptomatic) and have never received treatment OR are receiving the drug risdiplam.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for spinal muscular atrophy
Open Targets drugs acting on SIGMAR1
The Clinical Development of Taldefgrobep Alfa: An Anti-Myostatin Adnectin for the Treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
papers.summary: Taldefgrobep alfa binds and suppresses myostatin, increasing thigh muscle volume or lean body mass in healthy volunteers and producing modest muscle-mass gains in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, but it did not improve Duchenne motor function or meet the prespecified NSAA futility threshold. The paper mentions apitegromab as an anti-myostatin therapy studied in spinal muscular atrophy, but provides no clinical data for that spinal muscular atrophy trial.
papers.why: Although studied in Duchenne muscular dystrophy, the anti-myostatin therapy and muscle-function endpoints provide clinically tested approaches that may transfer to the muscle atrophy phenotype of SMA.

papers.title: ActRIIB blockade increases force-generating capacity and preserves energy supply in exercising mdx mouse muscle in vivo.
papers.summary: In dystrophic mdx mice, 8 weeks of soluble ActRIIB-Fc treatment increased gastrocnemius muscle volume by 33% and maximum absolute contractile force by 40% during standardized fatiguing exercise. Specific force, fatigue resistance, ATP homeostasis, and contractile efficiency were unchanged, while intrinsic mitochondrial ATP-producing capacity was reduced, indicating that increased muscle mass did not correct the fundamental weakness of dystrophic muscle.

papers.title: Treatment with soluble activin type IIB-receptor improves bone mass and strength in a mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In male mdx mice with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, the soluble activin type IIB-receptor decoy ActRIIB-Fc increased skeletal-muscle mass, bone mass and quality, and long-bone strength while reducing osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. ActRIIB-Fc inhibits both activin A and myostatin, but the study could not determine which ligand produced the skeletal effects, and voluntary running added no significant benefit to ActRIIB-Fc treatment.

papers.title: Inhibition of activin-like kinase 4/5 attenuates cancer cachexia associated muscle wasting.
papers.summary: ALK4/5 inhibition, particularly with GW788388, enhanced C2C12 myogenesis and preserved skeletal-muscle mass, strength, and body weight in the C26-CD2F1 cancer-cachexia model while reducing Atrogin-1 expression. These findings support pharmacological blockade of the myostatin signaling pathway as a transferable approach to muscle wasting, whereas LONG R3 IGF-I did not improve strength and showed an unfavorable trend toward tumor growth.

papers.title: Inhibiting myostatin signaling partially mitigates structural and functional adaptations to hindlimb suspension in mice.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6J mice subjected to 14 days of hindlimb suspension, an anti-myostatin peptibody partially preserved skeletal-muscle mass and increased fast-twitch fiber cross-sectional area, but did not significantly restore in vivo hindlimb force or soleus tetanic force in suspended mice. The treatment did not significantly reduce Atrogin-1 or MuRF-1 expression or increase Akt or p70S6K activation, indicating that myostatin is only one contributor to disuse-induced muscle wasting.

papers.title: Mathematical Model of Muscle Wasting in Cancer Cachexia.
papers.summary: The paper presents an ordinary-differential-equation model, parameterized with C26 mouse data, of myostatin/activin A/ActRIIB signaling during cancer cachexia and sActRIIB treatment. Model fitting predicts that blocking this pathway partially restores muscle mass mainly by reactivating satellite cells, although tumor growth is unaffected and recovery remains incomplete.

papers.title: Activation of fast skeletal muscle troponin as a potential therapeutic approach for treating neuromuscular diseases.
papers.summary: CK-2017357 selectively sensitized the fast skeletal troponin complex to calcium and increased skeletal muscle force at submaximal stimulation rates. In the passive-transfer experimental autoimmune myasthenia gravis rat model, a single dose immediately improved muscle force, reduced use-dependent fatigue, and increased grip strength, supporting transfer of this distal contractility approach to disorders such as spinal muscular atrophy.

papers.title: Fast skeletal muscle troponin activator tirasemtiv increases muscle function and performance in the B6SJL-SOD1G93A ALS mouse model.
papers.summary: In the B6SJL-SOD1G93A mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, the fast skeletal troponin activator tirasemtiv acutely improved submaximal EDL and diaphragm force, forelimb grip, grid-hang time, rotarod performance, and tidal volume. Benefits were stage-dependent and were generally absent from conscious functional tests after more advanced weakness, while chronic treatment did not harm survival and modestly prolonged time to humane endpoint in a post-hoc pooled analysis.

papers.title: Pathogenic variants in TNNC2 cause congenital myopathy due to an impaired force response to calcium.
papers.summary: This paper reports that pathogenic TNNC2 variants cause a dominantly inherited congenital myopathy by impairing the calcium-dependent force response of skeletal muscle sarcomeres. Replacement of mutant troponin C with recombinant wild-type troponin C repaired contractile dysfunction in patient myofibers, and tirasemtiv also repaired the dysfunction, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for skeletal muscle contractility.

papers.title: Zebrafish orthologs of human muscular dystrophy genes.
papers.summary: This paper identifies and maps zebrafish orthologs of 25 human muscular dystrophy-associated genes and four additional myopathy-associated genes, providing a resource for candidate-gene discovery in zebrafish dystrophy mutants. It also supports zebrafish as a model for genetic and small-molecule screens relevant to dystrophy, but it does not directly test therapies for spinal muscular atrophy or demonstrate effects on skeletal muscle contractility.

papers.title: Targeting MuRF1 by small molecules in a HFpEF rat model improves myocardial diastolic function and skeletal muscle contractility.
papers.summary: In obese ZSF1 rats with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, the MuRF1-targeting small molecule MyoMed-205 improved skeletal muscle force, attenuated muscle atrophy, reduced MuRF1 content and muscle protein ubiquitination, and increased mitochondrial respiratory-chain protein synthesis and enzyme activity. The intervention did not improve muscle fatigability or normalized specific force in soleus muscle, and its applicability to longer-term human treatment remains uncertain because of possible MuRF1-related cardiotoxicity.

papers.title: Troponin activator augments muscle force in nemaline myopathy patients with nebulin mutations.
papers.summary: In permeabilised skeletal muscle cells from nemaline myopathy patients with nebulin mutations, the fast skeletal muscle troponin activator CK-2066260 increased the calcium-sensitivity of force generation beyond untreated control levels without changing activation cooperativity. The findings support fast skeletal troponin activation as a mechanism for augmenting skeletal muscle contractility in nemaline myopathy and potentially other neuromuscular diseases.

papers.title: Synapse-specific Lrp4 mRNA enrichment requires Lrp4/MuSK signaling, muscle activity and Wnt non-canonical pathway.
papers.summary: The study identifies an agrin/Lrp4/MuSK-dependent mechanism that concentrates Lrp4 mRNA at the neuromuscular junction and shows that muscle activity and non-canonical Wnt/ROCK signaling also regulate this process. ROCK inhibition with RKI-1447 reduces basal and Wnt-induced Lrp4 expression and diminishes synaptic Lrp4 reporter activity in adult mouse muscle, while electrical stimulation restores synaptic localization in aged muscle.

papers.title: Patient-specific therapeutic benefit of MuSK agonist antibody ARGX-119 in MuSK myasthenia gravis passive transfer models.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the bivalent MuSK agonist antibody ARGX-119 ameliorates MuSK myasthenia gravis in one of four patient-IgG4 passive-transfer mouse models, with a bell-shaped dose-response and no significant benefit in the other three models. A C2C12 myotube AChR-clustering assay tracked the in vivo response and may help identify ARGX-119-sensitive patients, but requires clinical validation.

papers.title: Muscle specific kinase (MuSK) activation preserves neuromuscular junctions in the diaphragm but is not sufficient to provide a functional benefit in the SOD1G93A mouse model of ALS.
papers.summary: Chronic treatment of SOD1 G93A mice with a MuSK agonist antibody fully preserved diaphragm neuromuscular-junction innervation but did not preserve diaphragm function, motor neurons, or survival. The findings indicate that anatomical neuromuscular-junction preservation through MuSK activation does not provide functional benefit in this ALS model.

papers.title: The MuSK agonist antibody protects the neuromuscular junction and extends the lifespan in C9orf72-ALS mice.
papers.summary: The study shows that poly-PR proteins expressed in motor neurons disrupt Agrin–Lrp4 interaction and reduce MuSK activation, causing neuromuscular-junction deficits in HB9-PR F/F C9orf72-ALS mice. A MuSK agonist antibody rescued neuromuscular-junction deficits and extended lifespan, providing a therapeutic strategy centered on agrin/Lrp4/MuSK signaling.

papers.title: Schwann cell-specific PTEN and EGFR dysfunctions affect neuromuscular junction development by impairing Agrin signaling and autophagy.
papers.summary: This mouse study shows that Schwann cell-specific Pten inactivation or EGFR overexpression causes neuromuscular-junction malformation, reduced Agrin signaling in tibialis anterior muscle, and altered signaling and autophagy in sciatic nerves. Torin 2, an mTOR inhibitor, rescued the phenotype, supporting a mechanistic role for impaired autophagy in the Agrin-signaling abnormality.

papers.title: Collagen Q and anti-MuSK autoantibody competitively suppress agrin/LRP4/MuSK signaling.
papers.summary: The paper shows that MuSK-IgG and the C-terminal domain of collagen Q both suppress agrin/LRP4/MuSK signaling; patient-derived MuSK-IgG suppressed signaling about twice as strongly as recombinant ColQ CTD. MuSK-IgG also reduced acetylcholine receptor clustering in Colq-knockout mice, showing that direct blockade of MuSK-LRP4 binding is a primary cause of the signaling defect in this myasthenia gravis model.

papers.title: Transgenic rescue of neurogenic atrophy in the nmd mouse reveals a role for Ighmbp2 in dilated cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: The paper shows that restoring full-length Ighmbp2 expression in neurons prevents primary motor-neuron degeneration and restores axonal morphology and density in nmd mice. Reduced IGHMBP2 is associated with neurogenic atrophy and dilated cardiomyopathy, but the paper does not investigate or provide interventions targeting RNA–DNA hybrids.

papers.title: ATM pathway activation limits R-loop-associated genomic instability in Werner syndrome cells.
papers.summary: In Werner syndrome fibroblasts, WRN loss causes accumulation of RNA–DNA hybrids that impair replication-fork progression, undergo XPG-dependent processing, and activate ATM signaling. Direct or indirect suppression of RNA–DNA hybrid formation reduced DNA damage and chromosomal aberrations, whereas ATM inhibition aggravated these outcomes, providing an experimentally supported intervention strategy with potential mechanistic transfer.

papers.title: Sae2/CtIP prevents R-loop accumulation in eukaryotic cells.
papers.summary: The paper shows that loss or depletion of Sae2 in yeast or CtIP in human U2OS cells causes transcription-associated stalling and accumulation of RNA–DNA hybrids, especially after genotoxic stress. Sen1/Senataxin or RNaseH overexpression suppresses these defects and improves survival, while complementary transcription-factor and transcription-inhibition approaches provide additional, context-dependent rescue.

papers.title: USP11 controls R-loops by regulating senataxin proteostasis.
papers.summary: The study shows that USP11 loss, through increased K48-ubiquitination and degradation of SETX, causes accumulation of DNA:RNA hybrids (R-loops) in human cells, followed by XPF-associated double-strand breaks and hypersensitivity to DNA-damaging agents. RNase H1 overexpression reverses R-loop accumulation and suppresses the associated DNA damage and drug hypersensitivity, while wild-type USP11 but not its catalytically inactive mutant restores R-loop homeostasis.

papers.title: DHX9 SUMOylation is required for the suppression of R-loop-associated genome instability.
papers.summary: The study shows that SUMO2/3 modification of DHX9 at K120 promotes its association with RNA–DNA hybrids and RNA-processing proteins, thereby limiting R-loop accumulation, DNA damage, and cell death. RNase H overexpression or fusion of SUMO2 to the SUMOylation-deficient DHX9 K120R mutant rescued these defects, but the helicase activity of DHX9 was unchanged.

papers.title: RadD Contributes to R-Loop Avoidance in Sub-MIC Tobramycin.
papers.summary: Sub-MIC tobramycin induces translation defects and proposed RNA–DNA hybrid/R-loop accumulation, leading to DNA double-strand breaks that require RecBCD-mediated homologous recombination when RadD is absent. RNase H1 overexpression reduced DNA breaks and restored growth, whereas RadD overexpression reduced an R-loop-dependent replication phenotype, although RadD’s direct activity on RNA–DNA hybrids was not demonstrated.

papers.title: Caffeine mitigates ROS accumulation and attenuates motor neuron degeneration in the wobbler mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.summary: In the Wobbler mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, caffeine supplementation from symptom onset reduced reactive oxygen species, restored spinal-cord NAD+ levels, and preserved cervical motor neurons without increasing NMNAT2 expression. Functional grip-strength benefit was transient, forelimb strength and soma morphology were unchanged, and longer-term protection or translation to human disease remains unresolved.

papers.title: Intravenous administration of an engineered AAV9-gene-silencing vector suppresses human SOD1 and extends survival in an ALS mouse model.
papers.summary: A single intravenous dose of an engineered AAV9 vector expressing dual SOD1-targeting artificial microRNAs under the human SMN1 promoter reduced human SOD1 throughout central and peripheral tissues of SOD1G93A ALS mice. Treatment preserved motor neurons and neuromuscular junctions, improved respiratory and motor outcomes, reduced serum neurofilament light chain, and extended survival even when initiated after disease onset, but efficacy and safety in humans remain unestablished.

papers.title: LXR Pathway Activation by T0901317: A Novel Potential Experimental Strategy for ALS-Related Cognitive and Motor Impairments via Suppression of Necroptosis-associated RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL Markers.
papers.summary: In TDP-43-A315T ALS cell and mouse models, the non-selective LXR agonist T0901317 reduced TDP-43 aggregation and RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL necroptosis signaling, while protecting against motor neuron degeneration, muscle atrophy, and cognitive and motor deficits. LXR antagonism with GSK2033 abolished or reversed these effects, but pathway engagement and the relative contributions of apoptosis versus necroptosis were not definitively established.

papers.title: Fatty acid amide hydrolase inhibition for treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.summary: This paper identifies elevated serum N-acyl taurines as biomarkers associated with rapid progression and shorter survival in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The fatty acid amide hydrolase inhibitor PF-04457845 increases N-acyl taurines and N-acyl ethanolamines and protects motor neurons in ALS cellular models and SOD1G93A mice through glial and neuronal mechanisms, but it was not tested as an ALS treatment in patients.

papers.title: A gut-activated NHR-86-CYP pathway mediates the neuroprotective effects of Enterococcus faecium probiotics in a nematode model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
papers.summary: In Caenorhabditis elegans models carrying ALS-associated sod-1 mutations, live Enterococcus faecium protected cholinergic motor neurons from paraquat-induced degeneration and improved survival and locomotion. The protective effect required intestinal NHR-86-dependent induction of cytochrome P450 genes, which reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species; canonical immune pathways were not required.

papers.title: Site-targeted proximal complement C3 inhibition, but not C5 blockade, attenuates neurodegeneration in a mouse model of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis: Implications for failed clinical trials.
papers.summary: In hSOD1G93A mice with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, site-targeted complement C3 inhibition with CR2Crry attenuated neuroinflammation, preserved motor neurons and peripheral axons, maintained neuromuscular junctions, improved selected functional outcomes, and extended survival. In contrast, C5 blockade with BB5.1 suppressed membrane attack complex deposition but produced no significant structural, functional, or survival benefit, indicating that proximal C3 activation rather than terminal C5a or membrane attack complex activity was the dominant treatment-responsive mechanism in this model.

unread.title: ATP7A Clinical Genetics Resource - A comprehensive clinically annotated database and resource for genetic variants in ATP7A gene.
unread.why: Offers a clinically annotated ATP7A variant database and interpretation tools directly relevant to ATP7A-associated X-linked distal spinal muscular atrophy.

unread.title: Mutations in BICD2, which encodes a golgin and important motor adaptor, cause congenital autosomal-dominant spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Identifies pathogenic BICD2 variants in dominant SMA and supplies cellular and patient-derived experimental models with functional readouts.

unread.title: Mutations in BICD2 cause dominant congenital spinal muscular atrophy and hereditary spastic paraplegia.
unread.why: Provides functional assays and mechanistic evidence for BICD2-related dominant congenital SMA and motor-neuron trafficking.

unread.title: Phenotypic and molecular insights into spinal muscular atrophy due to mutations in BICD2.
unread.why: A detailed BICD2-SMA cohort and natural-history characterization provide reusable outcome measures, imaging protocols, and disease models.

unread.title: Expanding the phenotype of BICD2 mutations toward skeletal muscle involvement.
unread.why: Reports functional cellular and ultrastructural assays for BICD2-related skeletal-muscle disease that can be applied to relevant SMA models.

unread.title: Nusinersen versus Sham Control in Infantile-Onset Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: A phase III trial directly demonstrates nusinersen's efficacy in infantile-onset SMA and validates clinically meaningful motor and survival endpoints.

unread.title: Mid- and long-term (at least 12 months) follow-up of patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) treated with nusinersen, onasemnogene abeparvovec, risdiplam or combination therapies: A systematic review of real-world study data.
unread.why: A systematic review summarizes real-world efficacy, safety, and motor outcomes for approved and combination SMA treatments.

unread.title: How does risdiplam compare with other treatments for Types 1-3 spinal muscular atrophy: a systematic literature review and indirect treatment comparison.
unread.why: Compares existing approved SMA therapies using individual and aggregate clinical data, including survival and motor-function outcomes.

unread.title: Efficacy of risdiplam in spinal muscular atrophy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
unread.why: A meta-analysis provides quantitative evidence for risdiplam effects and identifies reusable motor and respiratory outcome measures in SMA.

unread.title: Scapuloperoneal spinal muscular atrophy and CMT2C are allelic disorders caused by alterations in TRPV4.
unread.why: Provides a functional assay and causal mechanism for TRPV4-related scapuloperoneal spinal muscular atrophy, a directly relevant SMA phenotype.

unread.title: Microscopic and Biochemical Hallmarks of BICD2-Associated Muscle Pathology toward the Evaluation of Novel Variants.
unread.why: This study develops and validates muscle histopathology and proteomic markers for assessing BICD2-associated motor-neuron disease pathology and variant pathogenicity.

unread.title: Identification of proximal spinal muscular atrophy carriers and patients by analysis of SMNT and SMNC gene copy number.
unread.why: The study develops and validates a quantitative PCR assay for SMN copy-number determination, carrier detection, and differentiation of SMA from phenocopies.

unread.title: Reduced SMN protein impairs maturation of the neuromuscular junctions in mouse models of spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Using SMA mice and patient tissue, the paper establishes early neuromuscular-junction defects and candidate biomarkers relevant to therapeutic research.

unread.title: SMN oligomerization defect correlates with spinal muscular atrophy severity.
unread.why: The study directly links a biochemical SMN self-association defect to clinical severity, providing a measurable candidate biomarker.

unread.title: Spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: This disease-focused review summarizes approved SMN-increasing treatments, supportive-care standards, and clinical outcomes relevant to accelerating SMA research.

unread.title: Genetic homogeneity between childhood-onset and adult-onset autosomal recessive spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: SMN deletion analysis is presented as a diagnostic approach that detects adult-onset as well as childhood-onset spinal muscular atrophy.

unread.title: A new method for SMN1 and hybrid SMN gene analysis in spinal muscular atrophy using long-range PCR followed by sequencing.
unread.why: The paper develops and validates a long-range PCR-sequencing method for detecting intragenic SMN1 mutations and hybrid genes in patients with SMA.

unread.title: Loss of BICD2 in muscle drives motor neuron loss in a developmental form of spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Conditional mouse models, patient fibroblasts, and a transport assay provide experimentally validated systems for studying BICD2-related SMA motor-neuron degeneration and muscle-mediated pathology.

unread.title: Genotype-phenotype relationship in 2 SMA III patients with novel mutations in the Tudor domain.
unread.why: The report uses molecular testing and copy-number quantification to characterize SMN1 variants and genotype-phenotype relationships in SMA type III.

unread.title: Spinal Muscular Atrophy
unread.why: This review directly identifies approved disease-modifying therapies, diagnostic testing, and clinical monitoring approaches for spinal muscular atrophy.

unread.title: Nusinersen versus Sham Control in Later-Onset Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: A phase 3 trial provides direct evidence that intrathecal nusinersen improves motor function in later-onset SMA and validates the HFMSE outcome measure.

unread.title: Safety, tolerability, and efficacy of a widely available nusinersen program for Polish children with Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: This prospective program study provides real-world efficacy, safety, and CHOP-INTEND outcome data for nusinersen treatment in children with SMA.

unread.title: Real-world experience with switch to onasemnogene abeparvovec after initial therapy with nusinersen or risdiplam.
unread.why: This real-world study directly evaluates switching children with SMA from nusinersen or risdiplam to onasemnogene abeparvovec and reports motor gains and safety outcomes.

unread.title: Real-world evidence of Nusinersen treatment for patients with spinal muscular atrophy in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia: Initial insights from the Saudi national spinal muscular atrophy program.
unread.why: This national real-world program documents nusinersen treatment outcomes across SMA types using multiple validated motor and functional endpoints.

unread.title: 6MWT can identify type 3 SMA patients with neuromuscular junction dysfunction.
unread.why: The study validates the 6-minute walk test as a simple indicator of fatigue and neuromuscular-junction dysfunction in ambulant type 3 SMA patients.

unread.title: Gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy: the Qatari experience.
unread.why: Nine children with SMA showed significant motor gains and short-term tolerability following onasemnogene abeparvovec gene therapy.

unread.title: Spinal Muscular Atrophy Treatments, Newborn Screening, and the Creation of a Neurogenetics Urgency.
unread.why: This review identifies three approved disease-modifying SMA treatments and newborn screening as existing tools for enabling rapid presymptomatic therapy.

unread.title: Safety and efficacy of gene therapy with onasemnogene abeparvovec in the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
unread.why: A meta-analysis of 250 SMA patients provides quantitative evidence of motor benefit and characteristic adverse events after onasemnogene abeparvovec.

unread.title: Nusinersen treatment of spinal muscular atrophy - a systematic review.
unread.why: Systematic-review data show that nusinersen improves survival without permanent ventilation and motor outcomes, especially when administered presymptomatically.

unread.title: Nusinersen for adults with spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Real-world data from 32 adults show nusinersen responsiveness and support HFMSE, 6MWT, and ALSFRS-R as monitoring tools.

unread.title: A case series evaluating patient perceptions after switching from nusinersen to risdiplam for spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: This observational case series provides patient-reported evidence comparing nusinersen and risdiplam and informs decisions about switching between them.

unread.title: Onasemnogene abeparvovec-xioi: a gene replacement strategy for the treatment of infants diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: The review describes the development, approval, clinical efficacy, and durable motor gains of AAV-based SMN1 gene replacement for infants with SMA.

unread.title: Inflammatory markers in cerebrospinal fluid of paediatric spinal muscular atrophy patients receiving nusinersen treatment.
unread.why: The study applies multiplex cytokine profiling to CSF and identifies IL-10 and MCP1/CCL2 as measurable markers for monitoring nusinersen-associated biological and inflammatory changes.

unread.title: An observational cohort study on pulmonary function in adult patients with 5q-spinal muscular atrophy under nusinersen therapy.
unread.why: A 38-patient adult cohort supplies pulmonary, motor, fatigue, and quality-of-life endpoints for evaluating nusinersen response over 30 months.

unread.title: Gene-based therapy for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy types 1 and 2 : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
unread.why: A large meta-analysis compares three existing gene-based SMA therapies using survival, ventilation, motor-function, and adverse-event outcomes.

unread.title: Real-world safety and effectiveness of nusinersen, a treatment for spinal muscular atrophy, in 401 Japanese patients: results from an interim analysis of post-marketing surveillance.
unread.why: Post-marketing surveillance of 401 treated patients provides real-world effectiveness, safety, and outcome-measure data for intrathecal nusinersen.

unread.title: Bridging the Gap: Gene Therapy in a Patient With Spinal Muscular Atrophy Type 1.
unread.why: A treated SMA type 1 case reports clinical improvement with onasemnogene abeparvovec and describes concrete molecular treatment options for individualized selection.

unread.title: Evaluation of the therapeutic efficacy and tolerability of current drug treatments on the clinical outcomes of paediatric spinal muscular atrophy type 1: A systematic review.
unread.why: The systematic review synthesizes outcome data for three approved SMA type 1 therapies across motor, respiratory, hospitalization, survival, and safety endpoints.

unread.title: Effect of nusinersen treatment on quality of life and motor function in adult patients with spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: The study provides longitudinal real-world evidence that nusinersen improves motor function, strength, and physical quality of life in adults with SMA.

unread.title: Fatal outcomes following onasemnogene abeparvovec in advanced-stage spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: This observational cohort provides efficacy, motor-response, and survival data for onasemnogene abeparvovec in advanced SMA and identifies treatment-selection cautions.

unread.title: Nusinersen induces detectable changes in compound motor action potential response in spinal muscular atrophy type 1 patients with severe impairment of motor function.
unread.why: The study reports long-term nusinersen treatment and identifies CMAP response as an objective indicator of response in severely impaired SMA type 1 patients.

unread.title: Risdiplam and nusinersen in spinal muscular atrophy: a descriptive real-world study on motor function outcomes in northwestern Iran.
unread.why: The prospective real-world study compares risdiplam and nusinersen effects on validated motor-function outcomes in children with SMA types 2 and 3.

unread.title: Changes in pNFH Levels in Cerebrospinal Fluid and Motor Evolution after the Loading Dose with Nusinersen in Different Types of Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: This SMA study reports pNFH changes after nusinersen loading and identifies measurable biomarker and motor-function variables associated with treatment evolution.

unread.title: X-linked spinal muscular atrophy in mice caused by autonomous loss of ATP7A in the motor neuron.
unread.why: The paper develops and validates a motor-neuron-specific Atp7a knockout mouse model reproducing progressive motor-neuron degeneration, denervation, muscle atrophy, and gait deterioration characteristic of X-linked SMA.

unread.title: Molecular and functional analysis of intragenic SMN1 mutations in patients with spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: This SMA study provides molecular diagnostic methods for identifying intragenic SMN1 mutations and experimental assays for testing how variants disrupt SMN-complex function.

unread.title: Phenotypic spectrum and incidence of TRPV4 mutations in patients with inherited axonal neuropathy.
unread.why: The study validates targeted TRPV4 screening and characterizes clinical and electrophysiological phenotypes in patients including congenital and scapuloperoneal SMA forms.

unread.title: Rescue of a Mouse Model of Spinal Muscular Atrophy With Respiratory Distress Type 1 by AAV9-IGHMBP2 Is Dose Dependent.
unread.why: The study directly demonstrates dose-dependent rescue of an IGHMBP2-deficient SMA-related mouse model using AAV9 gene replacement, improving survival, strength, neuromuscular junctions, and motor pathology.

unread.title: Altered intracellular localization and valosin-containing protein (p97 VCP) interaction underlie ATP7A-related distal motor neuropathy.
unread.why: Using ATP7A-associated distal motor neuropathy, a motor-neuron disease involving an SMA input gene, the study shows that siRNA depletion of p97/VCP corrects mutant ATP7A mislocalization.

unread.title: Phenotypic variability of TRPV4 related neuropathies.
unread.why: The study identifies novel pathogenic TRPV4 variants in TRPV4-related spinal muscular atrophy using sequencing and detailed clinical, electrophysiological, and biopsy assessments.

unread.title: Conditional knockout of the Menkes disease copper transporter demonstrates its critical role in embryogenesis.
unread.why: The authors developed a floxed mouse model that enables tissue-specific Atp7a deletion and directly models ATP7A-related disorders, including X-linked spinal muscular atrophy type 3.

unread.title: Exome Sequencing Identifies DYNC1H1 Variant Associated With Vertebral Abnormality and Spinal Muscular Atrophy With Lower Extremity Predominance.
unread.why: Whole-exome sequencing successfully identified a de novo DYNC1H1 variant in a patient with spinal muscular atrophy with lower-extremity predominance.

unread.title: A recurrent de novo DYNC1H1 tail domain mutation causes spinal muscular atrophy with lower extremity predominance, learning difficulties and mild brain abnormality.
unread.why: The study provides a recurrent DYNC1H1 variant and muscle-MRI patterns that distinguish DYNC1H1-related spinal muscular atrophy and are more diagnostically specific than muscle biopsy.

unread.title: Novel insights into SMALED2: BICD2 mutations increase microtubule stability and cause defects in axonal and NMJ development.
unread.why: The study supplies cellular and fly models together with functional assays demonstrating that BICD2 mutations increase microtubule stability and impair motor-neuron, neuromuscular-junction, and locomotor development.

unread.title: DYNC1H1 gene methylation correlates with severity of spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Decreased DYNC1H1 exon 37 methylation is identified and experimentally associated with severe versus mild SMA, providing a candidate prognostic severity biomarker.

unread.title: Combined Genome Sequencing and RNA Analysis Reveals and Characterizes a Deep Intronic Variant in IGHMBP2 in a Patient With Spinal Muscular Atrophy With Respiratory Distress Type 1.
unread.why: Provides a concrete genome-plus-RNA diagnostic workflow that identified and characterized a deep intronic IGHMBP2 variant in a patient with SMARD1.

unread.title: Modelling the pathogenesis of X-linked distal hereditary motor neuropathy using patient-derived iPSCs.
unread.why: The patient-derived iPSC motor-neuron model reproduces ATP7A deficiency, defective copper response, and motor-neuron axonal degeneration relevant to X-linked SMA.

unread.title: In Vitro Modeling as a Tool for Testing Therapeutics for Spinal Muscular Atrophy and IGHMBP2-Related Disorders.
unread.why: Reports a reusable patient-derived induced-neuron platform and shows in vitro rescue of SMA and IGHMBP2-related phenotypes by AAV9-mediated gene replacement.

unread.title: Fetal early motor neuron disruption and prenatal molecular diagnosis in a severe BICD2-opathy.
unread.why: Demonstrates prenatal molecular diagnosis of a de novo BICD2 cause of severe SMALED2B and quantitative neuropathologic assessment of fetal motor-neuron loss.

unread.title: Correlation between severity and SMN protein level in spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Directly demonstrates deficient SMN protein in SMA patients and establishes protein-level testing as a disease-related biomarker.

unread.title: Quantitative analysis of survival motor neuron copies: identification of subtle SMN1 mutations in patients with spinal muscular atrophy, genotype-phenotype correlation, and implications for genetic counseling.
unread.why: This study develops and validates molecular methods for quantifying and identifying SMN1 variants in nondeleted SMA patients and provides genotype-phenotype interpretation.

unread.title: Intravenous scAAV9 delivery of a codon-optimized SMN1 sequence rescues SMA mice.
unread.why: The study demonstrates a gene-therapy approach that substantially rescues motor-neuron loss, motor function, weight loss, and survival in an SMA mouse model.

unread.title: Multiplex digital PCR: breaking the one target per color barrier of quantitative PCR.
unread.why: The paper demonstrates a multiplex digital-PCR assay for simultaneous SMN1/SMN2 dosage and SMN1 variant detection, including testing in SMA patient samples.

unread.title: Impaired Muscle Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Myogenesis in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: The study directly quantifies mitochondrial dysfunction in muscle from multiple SMA subtypes using patient biopsies and provides assays for measuring this disease-relevant pathology.

unread.title: Multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification improves diagnostics in spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: The paper directly validates MLPA as a clinical diagnostic assay for detecting SMN1 deletions and copy-number variation in SMA.

unread.title: Molecular characterization of SMN copy number derived from carrier screening and from core families with SMA in a Chinese population.
unread.why: The study directly develops and validates a rapid SMA genotyping screen and reports a substantial population-level carrier and mutation dataset.

unread.title: Characterization of functional domains of the SMN protein in vivo.
unread.why: A conditional SMN-depletion DT40 cell system functionally tested SMA-associated SMN mutants and identified protein domains required for survival activity.

unread.title: Mutation Spectrum of the Survival of Motor Neuron 1 and Functional Analysis of Variants in Chinese Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: The study validates a molecular diagnostic workflow for detecting deletions, copy-number changes, and subtle SMN1 variants in a large Chinese SMA cohort.

unread.title: Involvement of survival motor neuron (SMN) protein in cell death.
unread.why: Cell-based survival and apoptosis assays directly compare wild-type and SMA-associated SMN proteins and identify the C-terminal region as necessary for anti-apoptotic function.

unread.title: A genetic and phenotypic analysis in Spanish spinal muscular atrophy patients with c.399_402del AGAG, the most frequently found subtle mutation in the SMN1 gene.
unread.why: The study shows in SMA patients that SMN2 copy number, SMN transcript output, and protein levels can inform genotype–phenotype interpretation and disease severity.

unread.title: Intragenic variants in the SMN1 gene determine the clinical phenotype in 5q spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: Large-cohort sequencing and copy-number analysis identify recurrent SMN1 variants and show that their effects on phenotype can differ from those of SMN2 copy number.

unread.title: Molecular diagnosis of non-deletion SMA patients using quantitative PCR of SMN exon 7.
unread.why: The paper combines a molecular diagnostic assay with direct evidence that aminoglycosides suppress SMN1 nonsense mutations and alter exon skipping in patient cells.

unread.title: Premature termination mutations in exon 3 of the SMN1 gene are associated with exon skipping and a relatively mild SMA phenotype.
unread.why: The study directly examines SMA patient mutations and reports aminoglycoside-mediated suppression of nonsense mutations and exon skipping in cultured cells.

unread.title: Clinical and molecular cross-sectional study of a cohort of adult type III spinal muscular atrophy patients: clues from a biomarker study.
unread.why: The study evaluates molecular biomarkers and clinical outcome measures in adult type III SMA and identifies disease duration and lean mass as important confounders.

unread.title: Clinical and radiological profile of patients with spinal muscular atrophy type 4.
unread.why: This SMA type 4 cohort validates functional, neurophysiological, genetic, and radiological measures as potential biomarkers and outcome measures for genetic-therapy studies.

unread.title: Systematic Review of Motor Function Scales and Patient-Reported Outcomes in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: This systematic review identifies 15 commonly used motor-function and patient-reported outcome instruments, including 11 with validation assessments, for monitoring SMA.

unread.title: Survival Motor Neuron Protein is Released from Cells in Exosomes: A Potential Biomarker for Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
unread.why: The study demonstrates reduced exosomal SMN protein in SMA fibroblasts, mice, and patient serum and proposes it as a measurable SMA biomarker.

unread.title: Phenotypes of SMA patients retaining SMN1 with intragenic mutation.
unread.why: The study analyzes 515 SMA-like patients using qPCR, MLPA, and DNA/RNA analysis to identify SMN1 mutations and assess phenotype severity.

unread.title: Mutation analysis of 419 family and prenatal diagnosis of 339 cases of spinal muscular atrophy in China.
unread.why: The study validates a multi-method genetic testing workflow and applies it to 419 SMA patients and 339 prenatal diagnoses with high diagnostic yield.

unread.title: Characterizing the molecular phenotype of an Atp7a(T985I) conditional knock in mouse model for X-linked distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMNX).
unread.why: The paper develops and validates a motor-neuron disease model for an ATP7A motor neuropathy, providing a potentially transferable model and molecular readouts for ATP7A-associated motor neuron disorders.

unread.title: Evaluation of cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers in pediatric patients with spinal muscular atrophy.
unread.why: This study identifies CSF CHIT1 as a candidate biomarker of treatment response and relates it to a clinical motor-function endpoint in pediatric SMA.
